thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: SERVICE api-hosted-eu-west1 - LB Targets Unhealthy (TLS handshake failures) — page fired to @oncall-sre (P0) <https://pagerduty.example/incident/INC12345|INC12345>

pagerduty: Alert routed to devon (primary oncall) — escalation in 5m if not acked.

devon: acked — I'm on it. seeing spike in 5xx from eu-west-1. grabbing context and runbook now.

alex: any recent cert or infra deploys in eu-west?

maria: I see a cert rotation job completed ~8m ago for api-hosted-eu-west1 (internal certs service). low-level logs show lots of `tls: handshake failure` on the LB -> targets health checks.

devon: confirming from LB metrics: target group health dropping to 0/3, `Unhealthy` reason = TLS handshake error. Customers hitting hosted API in eu-west see 502/524. global traffic steering still sending to eu-west.

kevin: support: we're getting customer reports — some tenants in EU seeing spikes in latency/timeouts. CS already triaging.

alex: quick mitigation -> can we remove eu-west targets from the ALB and failover to eu-central standby pool? That should stop errors and restore successful requests to standby region.

maria: we can do that. prepping `aws elbv2` commands. note: DNS TTL is 60s for the region-level steering; failover should be quick. but need to ensure sticky sessions not required for these customers.

devon: executing failover steps from runbook: 1) mark eu-west target group as draining / set desired count 0 2) update routing policy to prefer eu-central 3) monitor errors.

devon: ran `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attribute Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=30` then `aws elbv2 set-rule-priorities` to route traffic away. Targets are deregistering.

incident-bot: Action recorded by devon at 1872460085.

maria: while draining, I'm pulling sample `openssl s_client -connect <target-ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.local` — getting `140735293062144:error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number`. that indicates TLS handshake mismatch (client expecting TLS1.2+, server speaking plain or closed).

alex: that matches a bad cert or a backend process failing to do TLS. Could be the cert rotation produced an intermediate chain issue. check `/etc/ssl/` on targets or the cert service logs.

devon: I can see the cert-service logs: `GET /certs/api-hosted-eu-west1 -> returned PEM with missing intermediate` at 1872460018. So yeah probable bad chain.

maria: mitigation path: revert cert rotation for api-hosted-eu-west1 and re-run health checks, OR keep eu-west drained until we can reissue corrected cert. which do we want?

alex: short-term, keep eu-west drained to restore customer traffic; long-term, re-issue corrected cert and deploy to targets behind a canary.

devon: agreeing. will keep eu-west out of rotation. notify customers.

kevin: CS note: telling affected customers to retry — we've shifted traffic to eu-central. ETA for full restoration depends on how quickly cert-service can fix and redeploy, but customer-visible errors should drop now.

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert auto-escalation suppressed (acknowledged).

maria: starting cert revert now — `kubectl -n certs rollout undo deployment/cert-rotator --to-revision=2` (that's the last known good). applying to eu-west cluster only.

alex: if rollback doesn't fix chain, plan B: generate new cert with full chain and upload via cert service API: ```
POST /v1/certs/upload
{
  "name": "api-hosted-eu-west1",
  "pem_chain": "-----BEGIN...-----\n[full chain]\n-----END...-----"
}
```

maria: rollback completed to rev 2. re-checking target handshake... `openssl s_client` now returns full chain and `Verify return code: 0 (ok)`. restarting health checks.

devon: health is slowly returning: 1/3 -> 2/3 -> 3/3 healthy. ALB target group shows healthy.

incident-bot: system note: traffic steering adjusted back to prefer eu-west at 1872460450 (manual override by devon).

devon: switching traffic back now. running smoke tests on hosted API in eu-west.

kevin: CS update posted to status page: "Partial interruption in eu-west occurred due to certificate rotation issue; traffic failed over to eu-central for ~25 minutes. Service restored after rollback. We're investigating root cause and will follow up."

jordan: jumping in for handoff — devon, can you summarize current state for next shift?

devon: summary for handoff -> incident: P0 LB target TLS handshake failures after cert-rotator deploy; action: drained eu-west, failed over traffic to eu-central, rolled back cert-rotator to last good revision, verified chain and health, returned traffic to eu-west. Customer impact: ~25m of errors for eu-west tenants, affected metrics: 5xx spike and increased latency. Follow-ups: root cause of cert-rotator generating incomplete chain, add pre-deploy chain validation to cert-service, post-deploy synthetic checks for handshake.

jordan: thanks — I'll own follow-ups and remediation. creating issue and assigning to cert-team.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident resolved (partial) — monitoring for 30m. Incident record: <https://incidents.internal/INC12345|INC12345>.

devon: adding notes to the incident doc and tagging cert-team. great work everyone. :thumbsup:

maria: FYI DNS propagation looked fine — no recent changes to region DNS. this was strictly cert chain problem, not DNS. leaving this thread open until postmortem ticket is created.

kevin: support will follow up with affected customers and include timeline.

jordan: handing over to night shift. devon, if anything else pops up ping me.

devon: will watch metrics for 30m then close.

incident-bot: This thread archived to incidents channel at 1872460600.
